title: Competing-Recovery Haircut on Expected Capitation Recovery — Network Participation Agreements
content:
This Payment Integrity rule applies to the exit settlement of a Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement under the **Network Participation Agreements**. Recent overpayment notices compete for the same capitation payments, so the recovery Cascade expects from the payments still due is cut back.

**Rule.** The exit competing-recovery haircut is set by the agreement's overpayment notices dated fewer than 6 whole months before today:

- three or more lower the expected recovery by 20 percent;
- exactly two lower it by 10 percent;
- fewer than two lower it by nothing.

## How the haircut acts

Lowering the expected recovery by 20 percent means the expected recovery is multiplied by 80 percent; lowering it by 10 percent means multiplying it by 90 percent. The multiplication sits inside the single product that forms the expected recovery, which is rounded once, half up to the cent, at the end.

## Counting the notices

- Count the overpayment notices on the agreement whose notice date is fewer than 6 whole months before today.
- Whole months are the difference in calendar months from the notice date to today, less one when today's day of the month is smaller than the notice date's day of the month.

| Notices in the window | Expected recovery is multiplied by |
|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | 100 percent (no haircut) |
| 2 | 90 percent |
| 3 or more | 80 percent |

## Hypothetical illustration

Before any haircut, an expected recovery works out at 9000.00 USD. With three notices in the window, it becomes 7200.00 USD. With two, it becomes 8100.00 USD.
